test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two trains A and B of equal length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction with speeds of 64.8 km/h and 50.4 km/h respectively. Train A crosses train B in one minute. Find the length (in m) of each train.
solution:
Given:

When a train completely crosses another train, it basically crosses the sum of the lengths of the two trains.

Concept used:

Relative speed is the difference between individual speeds while two objects run in the same direction.

Distance = Speed × Time

When a train completely crosses another train, it basically crosses the sum of the lengths of the two trains.

Calculation:

Relative speed = 64.8 - 50.4 = 14.4 km/h

14.4 km/h = 14.4 ÷ 18/5 = 4 m/s

So, the sum of the length of train A and B = 4 × 60

⇒ 240 m

Now, the length of each train = 240/2 = 120 m

∴ The length of each train is 120 m.
